legend: - Imagine you have n%%ZSMJ0%% students lined up, each with an integer value. Your challenge is to split this line into one or more consecutive groups (the number of groups m%%ZSMJ1%% is not fixed) such that each group meets a special "hull" condition:
The first group starts with student 1%%ZSMJ2%% and the last group ends with student n%%ZSMJ3%%.
The groups are consecutive; if group j%%ZSMJ4%% covers students from index lj%%ZSMJ5%% to rj%%ZSMJ6%%, then for every 1≤j<m%%ZSMJ7%%, we have rj+1=lj+1%%ZSMJ8%%.
For each group j%%ZSMJ9%% (where 1≤j≤m%%ZSMJ10%%), if the group includes students with index lj,lj+1,…,rj%%ZSMJ11%%, then the sum lj+lj+1+⋯+rj%%ZSMJ12%% must be divisible by j%%ZSMJ13%%.
- Your task: Compute the number of ways to form such a segmentation of the students, and output your answer modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ14%%.
input: The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤n≤5∗103%%ZSMJ16%%) — the number of students.
output: Print a single integer: the number of valid segmentations, modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ17%%.
